Insights

Inventory is down 20% since Dec '25. Asking prices per living m² are up 8% to €4,985.

Map

Every listing, coloured by price per m². Hover for a photo, click to open it on Idealista.

Zones

The whole Mafra municipality, not just Ericeira. Distance to the sea sets the price more than the parish name.

Area & Price

Asking price against Área Útil by default, Área Bruta as a comparison. Smaller homes ask more per m², so compare like with like.

Agencies

Who lists what. A few agencies hold most of the listings, and each works a different price segment.

Efficiency

How much of the advertised area you can live in: Área Útil ÷ Área Bruta, by typology and agency.

History

Listings and median prices per m², month by month since we started tracking in December 2025.

Changes

Listing events since last month: new listings, removed listings, price reductions and increases. Removed does not mean sold.

iEach dot is a listing. The red trend line shows the typical asking price for each size. Dots below the line ask less than the trend for their size, dots above ask more. Asking prices, not valuations.
iHow property sizes are distributed. The red dashed line shows the median — half the properties are smaller, half are larger.
iHow listing prices are distributed. The red dashed line marks the median price.
iPrice per square metre normalises for size, letting you compare value across different properties.
iT0 = studio, T1 = 1 bedroom, T2 = 2 bedrooms, etc. Shows what’s most commonly available on the market.
iMedian price per m² for each property type. Error bars show the interquartile range (middle 50% of values).
iEach dot is a listing. The red trend line shows the typical asking price for each size. Dots below the line ask less than the trend for their size, dots above ask more. Asking prices, not valuations.
iHow property sizes are distributed. The red dashed line shows the median — half the properties are smaller, half are larger.
iHow listing prices are distributed. The red dashed line marks the median price.
iPrice per square metre normalises for size, letting you compare value across different properties.
iT0 = studio, T1 = 1 bedroom, T2 = 2 bedrooms, etc. Shows what’s most commonly available on the market.

iWhich agencies have the most listings in this area. More listings often means stronger local presence.
iMarket concentration: how much of the total supply is controlled by the top agencies vs. smaller ones.
iAverage listing price per agency. Helps identify which agencies focus on luxury vs. affordable segments.
iAverage price per m² per agency. A fairer comparison than total price since it accounts for property size.
iEfficiency = usable area ÷ gross area. 100% means all space is usable. Lower values mean more common areas, walls, etc.
iHow efficiency varies by property type. T0 and T1 perform best, but from T2 onwards efficiency becomes unpredictable: T3s in particular show the widest spread, meaning buying on gross area alone is a gamble.
iAverage efficiency by agency. Colour-coded: red = low efficiency, grey = near ideal. Count (n) shows sample size.
iCross-reference: efficiency by agency AND room type. Grey cells are closer to ideal; red cells indicate significant unusable space.

Ericeira Market Lens

A data-driven briefing on the Ericeira real estate market

This dashboard aggregates and visualises public listing data from Idealista for properties in the Ericeira area. It is designed to give a structured, at-a-glance overview of what is currently on the market, prices, surfaces, typologies, agencies, and space efficiency.

Disclaimer: This is not a valuation tool, a price forecast, or financial advice. All data comes from public listings and reflects asking prices, not transaction prices. Listings may contain errors, duplicates, or outdated information.

An opaque market

The Portuguese real estate market, and Ericeira in particular, is notoriously opaque. Transaction prices are rarely published, agency commissions vary widely, and reliable comparable data is hard to find. Buyers, sellers, and even professionals often navigate with limited visibility.

This project aims to reduce that asymmetry by making the publicly available listing data more accessible, structured, and comparable. It does not replace professional advice, but it provides a starting point for informed conversations.

For whom?

  • Buyers looking to understand the current supply and relative pricing
  • Sellers wanting to position their property against the market
  • Agents & advisors who need a quick market snapshot
  • Curious minds interested in Ericeira real estate dynamics

The focus is on relative positioning, not absolute truth.
See where a property stands compared to others, not what it is "worth".

Methodology

All prices on this site are asking prices taken from public listings. They are not recorded transaction prices.
Data source
Public listings on Idealista.pt under “comprar casas” (houses and apartments for sale), read from the search results and from each listing page.
Update frequency
Monthly. Each month uses the first complete scrape of that month; tracking started in December 2025.
Geographic scope
The scrape covers the whole Mafra municipality. Every tab except Zones is restricted to the Ericeira parish (freguesia), taken from the location in each listing’s title. The Zones tab shows all of Mafra, grouped by the zone Idealista assigns to each listing.
Inclusion
Every listing returned by the search for homes for sale in the area, whatever the asking price or size.
Deduplication
One row per Idealista listing ID per month. The same home advertised by two agencies under two IDs is counted twice; relisting detection is not applied yet.
How Área Útil is extracted
From the characteristics block of each listing page, where agencies state “m² úteis” (Área Útil) and “m² área bruta” (Área Bruta). Values are read as published, including thousands separators.
€/m² Área Útil
For each listing, asking price divided by Área Útil. The headline figure is the median across listings. €/m² Área Bruta is computed the same way, on the same listings, with Área Bruta.
Área Útil vs Área Bruta
Área Útil is the actual living space. Área Bruta is the advertised gross area and can include walls, garages, terraces, storage and other non-living areas, so €/m² on Área Bruta understates what living space costs and varies with how much extra area a listing includes.
Missing Área Útil
Listings that do not report both areas are excluded from the €/m² medians but kept in counts and in the median asking price. This month 346 of 449 listings (77%) report both, so the two KPIs are based on different samples.
Median changes
Monthly medians can repeat or jump when the middle of the distribution lands on the same listing. Treat changes over several months as more meaningful than a single month.
New listing
A listing ID present this month and absent from last month’s scrape.
Removed listing
A listing ID present last month and absent this month. It may have been sold, withdrawn, expired or relisted under a new ID. It is not treated as a sale.
Price change
A listing present in both months whose asking price changed by more than 0.5%.
First seen / months tracked
Scraping is monthly, so time on the market is counted in months in which the listing appeared. Listings already online in Dec '25 may have been listed earlier.
